title: Etale algebras over a henselian local ring have unique sections through rational points of the closed fibre
statement: Let $(S,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] (henselian in the sense of idempotent lifting for finite $S$-algebras), let $S\to B$ be a ring map such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $\mathfrak q'\subset B$ be a prime ideal lying over $\mathfrak m$ such that the induced map of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] $\kappa=S/\mathfrak m\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is an isomorphism. Then there is exactly one homomorphism of $S$-algebras $\sigma:B\to S$ (a retraction of $S\to B$) with $\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q'$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(8): proof reduces by Proposition Tag 00UE (proposition-etale-locally-standard) to a standard etale $S[t]_g/(f)$ ('details omitted'), lifts the simple root $a_0$ of $\bar f$ by the root-lifting definition of henselian (Definition Tag 04GF, definition-henselian), and gets uniqueness from Lemma lemma-uniqueness (just before 04GG). Stacks' definition of henselian is root lifting (04GF); [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] is idempotent lifting, so the split of this node also needs the equivalence (04GG (1)$\Leftrightarrow$(10), or More on Algebra Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex), (3)$\Leftrightarrow$(2): idempotent lifting for finite algebras is equivalent to lifting $A$-algebra maps $A'\to A/I$ from etale $A'$ to $A'\to A$, which gives existence directly)

proof.text: *The residue map $\rho$.* Write $\pi:S\to\kappa=S/\mathfrak m$ and $\iota:S\to B$ for the structure map. The composite $\kappa\to B/\mathfrak q'\hookrightarrow\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ [def-weil-residue-field] (the residue field of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ at $\mathfrak q'$ is the fraction field of the domain $B/\mathfrak q'$) is an isomorphism by hypothesis, so the subring $B/\mathfrak q'$ contains the image of $\kappa$, which is all of $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$; hence $S\to B/\mathfrak q'$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak q'\cap S=\mathfrak m$, and we get a surjective $S$-algebra map $\rho:B\to B/\mathfrak q'\cong\kappa$ with $\ker\rho=\mathfrak q'$. Moreover: (*) two surjective $S$-algebra maps $\psi_1,\psi_2:A\to\kappa$ from an $S$-algebra $A$ with the same kernel are equal, because $\psi_2=\alpha\circ\psi_1$ for a ring automorphism $\alpha$ of $\kappa$ which is $S$-linear, and $\kappa$ is generated by $1$ as an $S$-module, so $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. In particular, for an $S$-algebra map $\sigma:B\to S$ (a retraction, $\sigma\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_S$, so $\sigma$ and $\pi\circ\sigma$ are surjective) we have $\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\ker(\pi\circ\sigma)$, and $\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q'$ iff $\pi\circ\sigma=\rho$.

*Standard etale presentation (Stacks: by Proposition 00UE).* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-locally-standard] applied to $S\to B$ and $\mathfrak q'$ there are $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak q'$, a monic $f\in S[t]$, an $h\in S[t]$ with $f'p_1+fp_2=h^n$ in $S[t]$ (some $p_1,p_2\in S[t]$, $n\ge0$) and an $S$-algebra isomorphism $\varphi:B_g\xrightarrow{\sim}C=C(f,h)=S[t][Y]/(f,Yh-1)$; let $x\in C$ be the class of $t$ and $\lambda:B\to B_g$ the localization map. This is the only place where etaleness of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is used.

*Existence.* $S$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], so by [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] ((i)$\Rightarrow$(ii)), applied to the monic $f$ and the simple root $a_0$ of $\overline f$ (step 4), there is $a\in S$ with $f(a)=0$ and $\pi(a)=a_0$. Then $\pi(h(a))=\overline h(a_0)\neq0$, so $h(a)\notin\mathfrak m$ is a unit of the local ring $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-pair-maps] (1) with $L=S$, $b=a$, there is an $S$-algebra map $\tau:C\to S$ with $\tau(x)=a$. The $S$-algebra maps $\pi\circ\tau$ and $\rho_C$ from $C$ to $\kappa$ both send $x$ to $a_0$, so they are equal by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-pair-maps] (2) (determined by the image of $x$). By step 3, $\sigma=\tau\circ\varphi\circ\lambda:B\to S$ is an $S$-algebra map, i.e. a retraction of $S\to B$, with $\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q'$.

*Uniqueness (Stacks: 'By Lemma 06RR the map $\tau$ is unique').* Let $\sigma_1,\sigma_2:B\to S$ be $S$-algebra maps with $\sigma_i^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q'$. By step 3, $\sigma_i=\tau_i\circ\varphi\circ\lambda$ with $S$-algebra maps $\tau_i:C\to S$, $\pi\circ\tau_i=\rho_C$. Put $a_i=\tau_i(x)\in S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-pair-maps] (2) (with $L=S$), $f(a_i)=0$; $\pi(a_i)=\rho_C(x)=a_0$, so $a_1-a_2\in\mathfrak m$; and $\pi(f'(a_1))=\overline{f'}(a_0)\neq0$ (step 4), so $f'(a_1)\notin\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simple-root-uniqueness], $a_1=a_2$; so $\tau_1=\tau_2$ ([lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-pair-maps] (2): an $S$-algebra map out of $C$ is determined by the image of $x$), and $\sigma_1=\sigma_2$.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_algHom_of_henselianLocalRing_etale {S B : Type u} [CommRing S] [CommRing B] [HenselianLocalRing S] (φ : S →+* B) [AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ).op)] (q' : Ideal B) [q'.IsPrime] (hq : q'.comap φ = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) (hres : Function.Bijective (Ideal.ResidueField.map (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) q' φ hq.symm)) : letI : Algebra S B := φ.toAlgebra ∃! σ : B →ₐ[S] S, (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S).comap σ.toRingHom = q'
lean.note: The S-algebra structure on B is φ.toAlgebra, so the algebra retraction is of the same map used for étaleness and the induced residue-field map. HenselianLocalRing is the equivalent root-lifting notion recorded by the terminology dependency; Ideal.ResidueField is the canonical affine-scheme residue field.
